# Sharp weighted centroid tails fail under independent symmetric noise

The sharp triangle inequality
\[
 F(0)+F(s)+\lambda F(-s)\ge\Gamma+\lambda,\qquad
 \Gamma=\frac49,\quad\lambda=\frac79,
\]
proved in candidate 6c259b3f68b388b0
is NOT preserved by arbitrary independent symmetric additive noise.
An exact two-point counterexample works for every positive coefficient
\(\lambda\), including every \(0<\lambda\le7/9\) for which the original
uniform-triangle inequality is valid.

The failure also occurs for an actual full-dimensional product of a
centrally symmetric lattice polytope and a triangle, at its actual
integer-base centroid. That product nevertheless has exact maximal
normalized depth \(4/9\). These are obstructions to the stronger
weighted-tail preservation claim, not to OC.

## 1. One triangle direction

Let
\[
 T=\{(x_1,x_2):x_1,x_2\ge0,\ x_1+x_2\le1\},\qquad
 g=(1/3,1/3),
\]
and let \(X\) be uniform on \(T\). Put
\[
 Z=\frac{X_1+X_2}{2}-\frac13,\qquad F(v)=\Pr(Z\ge v).
\]
For \(q=1/3+v\),
\[
 F(v)=
 \begin{cases}
 1,&q\le0,\\
 1-4q^2,&0\le q\le1/2,\\
 0,&q\ge1/2.
 \end{cases}                                                   \tag{1}
\]
This follows by removing the similar origin triangle
\(x_1+x_2<2q\). Cut boundaries have zero area, so the formula is exact
for closed caps, including the supporting case \(q=1/2\).
The random variable \(Z\) has mean zero.

Take independent symmetric noise \(\xi=\pm t\), each with probability
\(1/2\), where
\[
 t=\frac16,\qquad s=\frac13.
\]
The six relevant tails are
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrr}
v&t&-t&s+t&s-t&-s+t&-s-t\\ \hline
F(v)&0&8/9&0&0&8/9&1 .
\end{array}                                                    \tag{2}
\]
Thus the proposed unaveraged noise inequality has left side
\[
 F(t)+F(-t)+F(s+t)+F(s-t)
       +\lambda[F(-s+t)+F(-s-t)]
   =\frac89+\frac{17}{9}\lambda,
\]
which is smaller than \(2(\Gamma+\lambda)\) by exactly
\[
 \frac{\lambda}{9}>0.                                         \tag{3}
\]
For \(\lambda=7/9\), the left side is \(191/81\), while the required
right side is \(198/81\); the strict gap is \(7/81\).

Equivalently, the centered noisy variable \(Z+\xi\) has tail
\(G(v)=[F(v-t)+F(v+t)]/2\), with
\[
 G(0)=\frac49,\qquad G(s)=0,\qquad G(-s)=\frac{17}{18}.
\]
Its weighted score is \(\Gamma+17\lambda/18<\Gamma+\lambda\).
The original paired-tail inequality is simultaneously sharp:
\(F(t)+F(-t)=2\Gamma\). Therefore preservation of the older paired
inequality cannot supply the stronger weighted conclusion.

For \(0<\lambda\le7/9\), validity of the original triangle inequality
follows from the sharp \(7/9\) result by decreasing its coefficient:
\[
 F(0)+F(s)-\Gamma\ge\frac79[1-F(-s)]
                       \ge\lambda[1-F(-s)].
\]
Hence (3) is a failure of preservation even when the starting inequality
is established, not merely a coefficient beyond its valid range.

## 2. Strict proper noisy cuts and continuous symmetric noise

The failure does not rely on a fragile supporting threshold.
Set
\[
 t_\varepsilon=\frac16-\varepsilon,\qquad
 s_\varepsilon=2t_\varepsilon,\qquad0<\varepsilon<\frac1{18}.
\]
Then
\[
 A:=F(t_\varepsilon)=4\varepsilon-4\varepsilon^2,\qquad
 B:=F(-t_\varepsilon)=\frac89-\frac43\varepsilon-4\varepsilon^2,
\]
while \(F(3t_\varepsilon)=0\) and \(F(-3t_\varepsilon)=1\),
strictly beyond their respective support endpoints. The unaveraged
weighted gap is exactly
\[
 2A+(1+\lambda)B+\lambda-2(\Gamma+\lambda)
 =-\frac{\lambda}{9}
   +\left(\frac{20}{3}-\frac{4\lambda}{3}\right)\varepsilon
   -(12+4\lambda)\varepsilon^2.                              \tag{4}
\]
It remains negative for all sufficiently small positive
\(\varepsilon\), for every fixed \(\lambda>0\).
All three noisy tails at \(0,\pm s_\varepsilon\) are strictly between
zero and one.

For the completely rational choice \(\lambda=7/9,\varepsilon=1/100\),
\[
 t_\varepsilon=\frac{47}{300},\quad
 s_\varepsilon=\frac{47}{150},\quad
 A=\frac{99}{2500},\quad B=\frac{19691}{22500}.
\]
The unaveraged gap in (4) is \(-3203/101250\), and the averaged noisy
tails are
\[
 G(0)=\frac{10291}{22500},\quad
 G(s_\varepsilon)=\frac{99}{5000},\quad
 G(-s_\varepsilon)=\frac{42191}{45000}.
\]
Their weighted score is \(244297/202500\), below \(11/9\) by
\(3203/202500\). All nonconstant component cuts are proper; the
remaining full/empty component cuts are strictly outside support.

There is also an absolutely continuous independent symmetric-noise
counterexample. In Section 1 replace \(\xi\) by
\[
 \xi+\eta,\qquad \eta\sim\operatorname{Unif}[-1/1000,1/1000]
\]
independently. Formula (1) shows that \(F\) is globally \(4\)-Lipschitz,
so each averaged tail changes by at most \(4/1000\).
The weighted score changes by at most
\[
 \frac4{1000}(2+\tfrac79)=\frac1{90}.
\]
Its original deficit is \(7/162\), leaving a deficit of at least
\(7/162-1/90=13/405>0\).
This noise law is symmetric and continuous, with two separated
intervals of support; no unimodality or log-concavity is asserted.

## 3. An actual centrally symmetric lattice-product source

For integer \(n\ge2\), define
\[
 P_n=\operatorname{conv}\bigl(
   \{1\}\times[0,1]^{n-1}\ \cup\
   \{-1\}\times[-1,0]^{n-1}\bigr).
\]
Its exact equivalent inequality description is
\[
 |z_1|\le1,\qquad |2z_j-z_1|\le1\quad(2\le j\le n).             \tag{5}
\]
Indeed, at real first coordinate \(q\in[-1,1]\), the convex combination
of its endpoint cubes gives the section
\[
 (P_n)_q=[(q-1)/2,(q+1)/2]^{n-1}.
\]
Thus \(P_n=-P_n\) and it is full-dimensional. Its integer points
have first coordinate \(-1,0,1\). At each endpoint there are exactly
\(m=2^{n-1}\) integer cube vertices; at zero there is exactly the
single integer point \(0\). There are no other integer points.

The body \(C=P_n\times T\) is an actual full-dimensional compact convex
body in \(n+2\) dimensions. It has exactly \(2m+1\) positive-area integer
fibers, every one equal to \(T\). Hence its normalized mixed law is
the product of uniform counting measure on \(P_n\cap\mathbb Z^n\)
and the uniform law on \(T\), and \((0,g)\) is an actual mixed centroid.

Use the genuine oblique scalar functional
\[
 Y=\frac{X_1+X_2}{2}-\frac13+\frac{z_1}{6}.
\]
The endpoint layers supply \(m\) copies of the pair in (2), while the
central layer supplies one copy of the original triangle law.
At \(s=1/3\), the central law has tails
\(F(0)=5/9,F(s)=0,F(-s)=1\), so its weighted score exceeds
\(\Gamma+\lambda\) by \(1/9\). Consequently the normalized product
gap is exactly
\[
 \frac{1-m\lambda}{9(2m+1)}.                                  \tag{6}
\]
For every fixed \(\lambda>0\), choose \(n\) with \(2^{n-1}>1/\lambda\);
then this actual lattice product violates weighted-tail preservation.
For \(\lambda=7/9\), already \(n=2,m=2\) suffices.

In that fixed-dimensional example the base is the parallelogram with
vertices \((1,0),(1,1),(-1,-1),(-1,0)\), with the origin as its sole
additional integer point. The exact product tails are
\[
 G(0)=\frac7{15},\qquad G(1/3)=0,\qquad G(-1/3)=\frac{43}{45}.
\]
Their weighted score is \(98/81<11/9=99/81\), a strict deficit \(1/81\).
All continuous cut boundaries are mixed-null; no vertical boundary
mass is removed in deriving these formulas.

## 4. Exact OC safety of the product

The product example has exact maximum normalized mixed depth \(\Gamma=4/9\).
At the actual point \((0,g)\), pair every nonzero integer base with its
negative. For a cap with nonzero continuous normal through this point,
the two triangle thresholds are opposite. The established ordinary
paired-centroid-tail theorem in
candidate 732b11a769399016 gives a combined
mass at least \(2\Gamma V\) for each pair, while the central triangle
gives at least \(\Gamma V\). Thus every such cap has fraction at least
\(\Gamma\). A closed vertical through-cap contains the central base and
at least one member of each reflected pair, hence has fraction at least
\((m+1)/(2m+1)>1/2>\Gamma\). Containing caps reduce to through-caps.

Conversely the three cylindrical caps defined by triangle barycentric
coordinates \(\lambda_i(x)\ge1/3\) cover the whole ambient space, because
\(\sum_i\lambda_i(x)=1\). Each has exactly fraction \(\Gamma\) in every
triangle fiber, hence in the entire product source. Every candidate
point therefore lies in a cap of fraction \(\Gamma\). This proves the
matching upper bound for all actual candidate points.
